audit.whatIsWrong: Content gave Xerath 6 of 7 rows against a 52.04% Aurelion Sol win rate, and rows 4, 5 and 6 disagreed with the full layer (Skill/Skill/Skill against Xerath/Xerath/Aurelion Sol).
audit.why: Xerath genuinely owns levels 1-5: Shocking Orb reaches 1050 and cancels both Aurelion Sol channels, and Arcanopulse pierces everything in its line so minions give no cover. From 6 the row is honestly even because Rite of the Arcane immobilises Xerath for its channel and Falling Star's stun ends it, and from two items the permanent Stardust curve passes his flat range-and-cooldown damage.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 Xerath, rows 4-5 Skill, row 6 Aurelion Sol, proposed as one atomic group with whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike and phase text named 'Mage Fire' (not a Xerath ability), plus 'Comet of Legend' and 'Starsurge' — both pre-rework Aurelion Sol abilities.
audit.why: Xerath's kit is Mana Surge (P), Arcanopulse (Q), Eye of Destruction (W), Shocking Orb (E), Rite of the Arcane (R). Aurelion Sol's is Breath of Light, Astral Flight, the black hole, and Falling Star into The Skies Descend.
audit.corrected: All three fabricated names replaced with the real abilities and the real spikes they describe.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two decisive interactions appeared anywhere: Shocking Orb cancels Breath of Light and Astral Flight mid-channel, and Rite of the Arcane is itself a channel that Falling Star interrupts.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol's Q and W both carry the interruptible-channel flag; Xerath's E carries hardCC and his R carries both hardCC and channel while immobilising him for its duration; Aurelion Sol's R carries hardCC.
audit.corrected: Stated in enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d, spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text, whys[4] and content mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit — the packet also flagged zero sequencing cues anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Real numbers exist: Shocking Orb 13/12.5/12/11.5/11, Eye of Destruction 14/13/12/11/10, Rite of the Arcane 130/115/100 at 5000 range.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around those three, with an explicit 'never start Q while Shocking Orb is up' sequencing line.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] told the reader to 'use E to block incoming Arcanopulse poke'. Aurelion Sol's E is a black hole; it blocks nothing.
audit.why: Riot's Arcanopulse text is 'dealing magic damage to all targets hit' — it pierces, so hiding behind the wave does not stop it either. Both halves of that advice were false.
audit.corrected: Replaced with movement advice that is actually true against a charged skillshot.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were other fields' strings pasted under unrelated titles; dontsFull[0].d, ahead, breakdown.carry and breakdown.feeding were name-swap templates.
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed and the template sweep.
audit.corrected: All eight rewritten from Xerath's kit at the same length.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane at 6 extends his range advantage into a global poke threat

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse and Mage Fire poke out-range your unstacked Q entirely, letting him zone you off CS and stack a gold lead before your orbit is threatening at all.
edits.after: Xerath's Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction out-range your unstacked Breath of Light, letting him zone you off CS while Shocking Orb cancels any channel you start in the open.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane fires from absurd range and can catch you across the lane or even snipe you during a Comet of Legend recall window, giving him poke pressure your kit can't answer at 6.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane fires from 5000 range and can catch you across the map, but it immobilises him for the whole channel — Falling Star's stun ends it, so hold R for the moment he casts.

edits.before: Once you're fully stacked with Comet of Legend online, your global pick threat and burst finally let you punish his positioning during fights, since his damage plateaus with items while your Q keeps scaling with every additional star.
edits.after: Once your Stardust turns Falling Star into The Skies Descend, your knockup drags him out of the artillery position he needs, since his damage plateaus with items while every Q tick you banked in lane still counts.

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse range simply outclasses your unstacked Starsurge, letting him poke you off CS and zone your farm from a screen away, and you have no real way to punish this until your own range and burst start to matter — expect to be behind on both gold and HP through the laning phase.
edits.after: Xerath's Arcanopulse outranges your unstacked Breath of Light, and Shocking Orb from 1050 cancels the channel the moment you start it, so he pokes you off CS from a screen away and you have no answer until your own range and burst matter — expect to be behind on gold and HP through laning.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane at level 6 extends his poke advantage into a genuine global-range threat, letting him snipe you during recalls or punish overextensions from absurd distance, and this poke war stays firmly in his favor even as you finish your first item, since his damage is range-and-cooldown based rather than a stat check you can outscale quickly.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane at 6 extends his poke into a 5000-range threat, letting him snipe you during recalls or punish overextensions from across the map — but the channel immobilises him and any hard CC ends it, so a held Falling Star turns his ultimate into your kill window rather than his, and the rest of the poke war still favours him.

edits.before: It takes reaching full stacks with Comet of Legend online for you to finally turn the corner — your global pick potential and stacked-Q burst let you punish his positioning in fights even though his poke never stops being annoying, and by two-plus items your scaling ultimately overtakes his flatter, range-dependent damage profile.
edits.after: It takes full Stardust and The Skies Descend for you to turn the corner — the knockup drags him out of the artillery seat his whole kit depends on, and by two-plus items your own scaling overtakes his flatter, range-dependent damage profile, even though the poke itself never really stops being annoying.

edits.before: Farm behind minions and use E to block incoming Arcanopulse poke
edits.after: Farm from max range and never stand still while Arcanopulse charges

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun) from 1050 range — it cancels your channel and every barrage after it lands for free.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Astral Flight has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and only 11s at rank 5 — it is his one piece of CC and it cancels your channel, so never start Q while it is up. - Eye of Destruction is 14s and slows you into the next Arcanopulse. - Rite of the Arcane is 100-130s and immobilises him: your R ends it.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by making range irrelevant: Xerath needs distance and a still target, and The Skies Descend gives him neither once your Stardust is banked.

edits.before: If Xerath takes first blood, tighten up: Shocking Orb (Stun) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with E executes and stay relevant through the stardust curve.
edits.after: If Xerath takes first blood his mana problem disappears and the poke never stops, so stop walking up at all: clear from 750 with the black hole, take the wave under tower, and only step out when Shocking Orb has been thrown.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Xerath on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, take his space: Xerath needs a still target at long range, so shove with E executes, fly at him on W, and make every wave a fight he cannot poke from.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Every second the breath stays on Xerath is permanent Stardust, and a 3s cooldown means you can restart it the instant he steps up.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Xerath for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: The black hole clears the back line from 750 range, so the wave dies without you ever stepping into the ground Arcanopulse actually covers.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Trading at his range means eating Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction for free.

edits.before: Your flight is your only escape — a W spent poking is a death sentence against the next gank.
edits.after: Shocking Orb reaches 1050 and cancels the channel — never start Q in the open while it is up.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1 and it is your only way out — flying at a Xerath with Shocking Orb up just delivers the stun.

One outright false mechanic fixed: wants.you[0] claimed Aurelion Sol's E blocks Arcanopulse — it does not, and Riot's own text says Arcanopulse damages all targets hit, so minions do not shield you either.
